scope: Independent GP-R1/GP-R2 front/rear contact force budgets and a speed-dependent AI braking horizon. Other motorcycles retain common contact grip and their current AI controllers. Equal-grip core trajectories match exactly. No snapshot protocol fields or integrated replay state added.

referenceContext.boundary: These observations constrain tire/contact presentation and leaned posture. They do not establish friction coefficients, tire wear laws or braking gains. All numerical tire coefficients and AI envelope margins remain existing simulation tuning.

contactReproduction.beforeDefinition: Common minimum front/rear grip used at both contact force circles in the baseline source.
contactReproduction.afterDefinition: Independent per-contact grip for the force circles; conservative minimum still used for intended lean.

brakingApproach.fixture: Production GP BikeAIDriver, BikeVehicle, Track, tyre and race/control code. Begins on the actual final straight 300 m before the start/finish at 90 m/s, on the racing line. Rain cases use wet tyres. Samples speed when crossing s600 and s650 on Poggio Alto; no force, pose or grip assistance is injected.
brakingApproach.horizon: Conservative full-stop distance from current speed and min(front/rear grip), plus existing 0.3 s lean-preview distance; bounded to fixed buffer capacity and one circuit.

productionRaces.configuration: Two laps; eight alternating GP-R1/GP-R2 entrants; normal production simulation at 120 Hz; AI demonstration enabled. The default medium compound and normal strategy/pit behavior are retained, including in the full rain race.
productionRaces.finalCriteria: Every rider classified with 2 completed laps, no retirement, zero crashes, zero contact impacts, zero penalties, finite snapshot.

resolvedInvestigations: Initial independent-contact code exposed a genuine GP AI regression: the 240 m shared preview could see a hairpin only after high-speed braking should have begun. In the clear Poggio Alto seed30101 race, rider2 ran wide into gravel near s678 and toppled at about137 race seconds. The current speed-dependent GP approach profile resolves this without disabling independent tyre contacts or relaxing crash thresholds.

The unchanged-baseline two-lap wet Poggio Alto race itself requires about548 simulated seconds. The first test cap of400 seconds could not establish classification. The final700-second cap accommodates the actual10.49 km course; all original crash/contact/penalty/classification assertions remain strict.

An exploratory90 m/s fixture placed a bike in the chicane preceding the final straight and put medium tyres into rain, triggering a crash/pit entry before reaching the measured approach. The final controlled approach fixture starts on the actual straight and uses wet tyres for rain.
validationBoundary: 30 new regression cases pass across focused executions; all12 existing GP control/passing cases also pass after the AI change. Whole-repository checks and graphics/browser verification are handled by the parent task. Simulation evidence does not establish measured real-MotoGP coefficients, physical-device performance, or subjective gameplay quality.
